newsitem.title: CHINA: China to strengthen quarantine under new rules.
newsitem.headline: China to strengthen quarantine under new rules.

text.p: China will tighten quarantine controls on animals and plants under new regulations that go into force on January 1, the China Daily said on Tuesday.
The rules would emphasise quarantine supervision since China quarantined less than five percent of the animal and plant products crossing its borders, the official newspaper said.
Chinese traders would be required to submit samples of relevant imports before signing contracts with foreign parties or shipping the goods, it said.

They would be barred from acquiring quarantine approval after the imports arrived in China, and commodities that came without approval would be burned or returned to foreign dealers, it said but gave no details.
The China Administration of Animal and Plant Quarantine had vowed to simplify quarantine procedures but not at the expense of sacrificing safety, it said.

Work aimed at keeping out foreign epidemics such as mad cow disease would be complicated in 1997 by the return to Chinese rule of the British colony of Hong Kong, which had little in the way of quarantines, it said.
The administration intended to boost checks at the Shenzhen border between Hong Kong and the mainland, China Daily quoted Director Yu Dahai as saying but did not elaborate.
